full_judgment: 6. From perusal of the judgment of the High Court Division it appears that the learned judges of the High Court Division affirmed the judgment and order of conviction and sentence of the accused-petitioners on the finding that there are sufficient evidence on record to hold that the accused-petitioners committed dacoity and that during commission of dacoity father of the informant was murdered. This finding of the learned judges of the High Court Division is based on legal evidence of PWs 1 and 2, who identified the accused-petitioners during TI parade and the order of conviction and sentence was maintained on the finding that during TI Parade PW 1 identified convict-petitioners and PW 2 identified Jalal Bepari and Ibrahim Sheikh and that after their arrest the petitioners brought out a single barrel gun and other materials of dacoity by digging earth from village Bandura PS Nawabganj District Dhaka. In view of such evidence (In record the submission of the learned Advocate for the petitioners that the confessional statements of the accused not having been relied upon by the courts below. and that non examination of the magistrate who held TI Parade are sufficient grounds to hold that the learned Judges of the High Court Division committed error in law in holding that the petitioners are guilty of the charges are of no substance. Mere placing no reliance upon confessional statement of the accused and non-examination of the Magistrate who held TI Parade are no ground for acquittal where the order of conviction and sentence is based on other sufficient and reliable legal evidence on record.
